newsitem.title: USA: Nintendo cuts N64 price to $149.95.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo cuts N64 price to $149.95.

text.p: Nintendo of America, a unit of Japanese video game maker Nintendo Co Ltd, on Monday said it cut the suggested retail price for its Nintendo 64 game player to $149.95 from $199.95.
In addition, the company said the installed base of Nintendo 64 (also called N64) machines, which were launched for the recent holiday season, has topped two million units.
"This new price point will make N64 available to even more game players in the U.S. and Canada," Peter Main, executive vice president of sales and marketing, said in a statement.

Nintendo said production efficiency from boosting planned global sales to 12 million units for the year starting April 1, 1997, along with favorable foreign exchange rates led it to make the price cut. But Nintendo is following closely on the heels of rival Sony Corp, which lowered its Sony Playstation video game player to $149 from $199 in early March.
In Japan, the company cut the price for N64 game players to 16,600 yen from 25,000 yen.
